title: 2000 AMC 10 Problem 22
statement: One morning each member of Angela’s family drank an \(8\)-ounce mixture of coffee with milk. The amounts of coffee and milk varied from cup to cup, but were never zero. Angela drank a quarter of the total amount of milk and a sixth of the total amount of coffee. How many people are in the family?

solutions.text:
Let there be \(n\) people, drinking \(8n\) ounces total, split into milk \(M\) and coffee \(C.\) Angela drank one cup, so \[\tfrac14 M + \tfrac16 C = \tfrac1n (M + C).\]

The left side is a weighted average of \(\tfrac14\) and \(\tfrac16,\) so \(\tfrac1n\) lies strictly between \(\tfrac16\) and \(\tfrac14.\) That forces \(4 \lt n \lt 6,\) so \(n = 5.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Angela’s cup is a fraction \(\tfrac1n\) of everyone’s total drink
Her cup is a mix of \(\tfrac14\) of the milk and \(\tfrac16\) of the coffee, so \(\tfrac1n\) lies strictly between \(\tfrac16\) and \(\tfrac14\)
